# Assignment 

**Goal 1**:

Combine the world shape `world` with:

  * Population (point) data (do not use rasters!)
  * Ports, airports, etc.

Produce:

  1. Map of total population by country
  2. Histogram of country population distribution by continent
  3. Histogram of (country-level) average distances between locations and ports or airports by continent.
  
**Goal 2**:

Read & download the [data](https://www.openicpsr.org/openicpsr/project/116359/version/V1/view) from the following paper:

  - Porteous, O., 2019. High trade costs and their consequences: An estimated dynamic model
    of African agricultural storage and trade. American Economic Journal: Applied Economics,
    11(4), pp.327-66. [Paper](https://www.jstor.org/stable/26794330)
    
Then, combine this data with world and transportation (e.g. road, railroad) data to:

  1. Generate an sf POINT feature of market prices places across Africa; plot them
  2. Calculate minimum distance of each market to the (i) coast, (ii) nearest road, and (iii)
nearest airport
  3. Produce 3 scatter plots relating average prices with the minimum distances
  
Our libraries for this assignment:

```{r libraries, include=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)   # dplyr, ggplot
library(patchwork)   # combine ggplots
library(sf)          # simple feature functions
library(spData)      # example geom sfs
library(spDataLarge) # example geom sfs (large)
```
  
# Part 1: Populations & Distances

*Notes from Bruno:*

  * For this task, you are required to obtain population data from a spatial (point) data set. There are many sources available for this, such as the "Populated Places" data set from Natural Earth.

  * Using this type of data is crucial for successfully completing the assignment. For instance, I expect you to calculate country-level population by linking this point data to the country shapes.

  * Similarly, I expect you to calculate the average distance between these locations (e.g., "Populated Places") and airports by combining the data sets and aggregating the statistics at the country level.

## 1. Map of total population by country

First, we will initialize our two data sets: 

  1. `world` from the `spData` library to serve as our world map of countries. 
  2. `countries` from the Natural Earth's library, specifically the [Populated Places](https://www.naturalearthdata.com/downloads/10m-cultural-vectors/10m-populated-places/) dataset.

```{r world and country data}
# world map from sf library
sf.world <- world %>% 
  rename(name = name_long) %>% 
  select(name, continent, geom)

# population data for cities around world
countries <- st_read("populated_places/ne_10m_populated_places.shp")
sf.countries <- countries %>% 
  select(NAME, POP_MAX, geometry) %>% # note CRS: WGS 84; matches world CRS
  rename(city = NAME, pop = POP_MAX, geom=geometry)
```

To generate a map of total population by country, we will combine these two `sf` objects using `st_intersect()`

```{r}
# merge world & country datasets by intersecting geometries
sf.country_pop <- st_join(sf.world, sf.countries, join = st_intersects)

# aggregate population by country
sf.aggregate <- sf.country_pop %>% 
  group_by(name) %>% 
  summarize(pop = sum(pop, na.rm=T))

# plot
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data=sf.aggregate, aes(fill=pop),
          color = "white", lwd=0.1) + 
  scale_fill_gradient( # gradient based on the country's population
    low = "#ffffb2",
    high = "#bd0026",
    name = "Country Pop",
    trans = "log10",
    labels = scales::label_number(scale_cut = scales::cut_short_scale()),
    guide = guide_colorbar(
    title.position = "left",
    title.hjust = 0.5,
    barwidth = 15,
    barheight = 0.4,
    order = 1)) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    # Legend
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.box = "vertical",
    legend.margin = margin(t = 10, b = 10, l = 10, r = 10),
    legend.box.margin = margin(t = -10, b = -10, l = 0, r = 0),
    
    # Image margins
    plot.margin = margin(t = 10, r = 10, b = 0, l = 10, unit = "pt"),
    
    # Text styles
    legend.title = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold", color = "grey20"),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 6, color = "grey30"),
    legend.key.size = unit(0.4, "cm")
  )

# note: populations arent entirely accurate -- likely missing a lot of rural data points 
sf.aggregate %>% 
  arrange(desc(pop)) %>% 
  head(n=5)

```



## 2. Histogram of country population distribution by continent

```{r}
# aggregate population by continent
df.aggregate<- st_drop_geometry(sf.aggregate) 
sf.aggregate_continent <- left_join(sf.world, df.aggregate, by = "name")

# histogram of pop by continent
df.aggregate_continent <- st_drop_geometry(sf.aggregate_continent)

# plots
df.aggregate_continent %>% 
  filter(pop > 0) %>% 
  ggplot(data=., aes(x=pop)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, aes(fill = continent), color = "white") +
  facet_wrap(~ continent,scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_number(scale_cut = scales::cut_short_scale())) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, color = "gray40"),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "gray90", colour = NA),
    panel.spacing = unit(1, "lines")
  )
```


## 3. Histogram of (country-level) average distances between locations (obs) and ports or airports by continent.

```{r port and airport data}
# airport data
sf.airports <- st_read("world_airports/ne_10m_airports.shp") # CRS: WGS84
sf.airports <- sf.airports %>% 
  select(name, featurecla, type, geometry) %>% 
  rename(size = type, feature = featurecla, geom = geometry)
# port data
sf.ports <- st_read("world_ports/ne_10m_ports.shp")          # CRS: WGS84
sf.ports <- sf.ports %>% 
  select(name, featurecla, geometry) %>% 
  rename(feature = featurecla, geom = geometry)
```


```{r airports}
# return every airport (pt) with associated country/continent
sf.airports <- st_join(sf.airports, sf.world, join=st_intersects)
sf.ports <- st_join(sf.ports, sf.world, join=st_intersects)
sf.travel <- bind_rows(sf.airports, sf.ports)

# return every city obs (pt) with associated country/continent
sf.cities <- st_join(sf.countries, sf.world, join = st_intersects)

# find closest airport/port to each city, store as indices
nearest_travel_indices <- st_nearest_feature(sf.cities, sf.travel)

# index sf.airport to get associated airport/port row-wise
closest_travel <- sf.travel[nearest_travel_indices, ]

# calculate distance b/w each city and the closest airport/port
dist_meters <- st_distance(sf.cities, closest_travel, by_element = TRUE)

# store in df
sf.cities$dist_to_travel_km <- as.numeric(dist_meters) / 1000
```


```{r histograms}
# aggregate by country:
sf.distances <- sf.cities %>% 
  group_by(name, continent) %>% 
  summarize(avg_dist_to_travel_km = mean(dist_to_travel_km, na.rm=T)) 

df.cities <- st_drop_geometry(sf.distances)

# plot histograms facet_wrapped by continent
df.cities %>% 
  filter(!is.na(continent)) %>% 
  ggplot(data=., aes(x=avg_dist_to_travel_km)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 20, aes(fill = continent), color = "white") +
  facet_wrap(~ continent,scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_number(scale_cut = scales::cut_short_scale())) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11, color = "gray40"),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "gray90", colour = NA),
    panel.spacing = unit(1, "lines")
  )
```



# Part 2: Marketplaces in Africa 


```{r datasets, include=FALSE}
rm(list=ls())

# World data
sf.world <- world %>% 
  select(name_long, continent, geom) %>% 
  rename(country=name_long)

# Africa roads
sf.roads <- st_read("groads-africa/gROADS-v1-africa.shp")
sf.roads <- sf.roads %>% 
  select(ROADID, LENGTH_KM, geometry)

# World railroads
sf.railroads <- st_read("world_railroads/ne_10m_railroads.shp")

# World airports 
sf.airports <- st_read("world_airports/ne_10m_airports.shp") # CRS: WGS84
sf.airports <- sf.airports %>% 
  select(name, featurecla, type, geometry) %>% 
  rename(size = type, feature = featurecla, geom = geometry)

# World Coastlines
sf.coastlines <- st_read("world_coastlines/ne_10m_coastline.shp") %>% 
  select(featurecla, geometry)

# Marketplace coords
df.marketplaces <- read_excel("MktCoords.xlsx")
sf.marketplaces <- st_as_sf(df.marketplaces,
                 coords = c('longitude', 'latitude'),
                 crs = 'EPSG:4326')

# Marketplace prices
df.marketprices <- read_excel("MktPrices.xlsx")

df.marketprices <- df.marketprices %>% 
  mutate(across(`1`:`144`, ~ na_if(., 0)),
         price = rowMeans(pick(`1`:`144`), na.rm=T)) %>% 
  select(-c(`1`:`144`))

```

```{r markets}
# combine sf.marketplace with `world` and transportation (roads, raildroads)
sf.marketplaces2 <- st_join(sf.marketplaces, sf.world, join=st_intersects)

# combine marketplaces + market prices
sf.markets_full <- sf.marketplaces2 %>% 
  left_join(., df.marketprices, by = c("market", "mktcode"))

```

## 1. Generate an sf POINT feature of marketplace across Africa; plot them

```{r}
# select world, filter only africa as background. then overlay our full markets data
sf.africa <- sf.world %>% 
  filter(continent == "Africa")

# plot
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data=sf.africa, color = "white", fill = "gray") +
  geom_sf(data=sf.markets_full, color = "darkred") + 
  labs(title = "Marketplaces across Africa") +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    plot.title =  element_text(hjust=0.5)
  )


```


## 2. Calculate minimum distance of each market to the (i) coast, (ii) nearest road, and (iii) nearest airport


```{r airports distances}
# three separate measurements; airports, roads, and coastlines

# filter for only airports in africa
sf.airports_africa <- st_filter(sf.airports, sf.africa, .predicate = st_intersects)

# sanity test
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data=sf.africa, color = "white", fill = "gray") +
  geom_sf(data=sf.airports_africa, color = "darkblue") +
  labs(title="Airports across Africa") +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust=0.5)
  )

# closest airport to a market, as a row index
closest_airport_index <- st_nearest_feature(sf.markets_full, sf.airports_africa)

# index the airport data to access the airport row (w/ the geom)
closest_airport <- sf.airports_africa[closest_airport_index,]

# find distance b/w closest airport and the associated marketplace
distances <- st_distance(sf.markets_full, closest_airport, by_element = T)

# convert meters to kilometers
dist_to_nearest_airport_km <- as.numeric(distances) / 1000

# append back to our marketplace simple feature object
sf.markets_full$dist_to_nearest_airport_km <- dist_to_nearest_airport_km

```



```{r roads distances}
# confirm data is roads only in Africa
sf.roads_africa <- st_filter(sf.roads, sf.africa, .predicate = st_intersects)

# sanity test
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data=sf.africa, color = "white", fill = "gray") +
  geom_sf(data=sf.roads_africa, color = "darkblue") +
  labs(title="Roads across Africa") +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust=0.5)
  )

# closest airport to a market, as a row index
closest_road_index <- st_nearest_feature(sf.markets_full, sf.roads_africa)

# index the airport data to access the airport row (w/ the geom)
closest_road <- sf.roads_africa[closest_road_index,]

# find distance b/w closest airport and the associated marketplace
distances <- st_distance(sf.markets_full, closest_road, by_element = T)

# convert meters to kilometers
dist_to_nearest_road_km <- as.numeric(distances) / 1000

# append back to our marketplace simple feature object
sf.markets_full$dist_to_nearest_road_km <- dist_to_nearest_road_km

```



```{r closest coastline}
# filter for only african coastlines
sf.coastlines_africa <- st_filter(sf.coastlines, sf.africa, .predicate = st_intersects)

# sanity test
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data=sf.africa, color = "white", fill = "gray") +
  geom_sf(data=sf.coastlines_africa, color = "darkblue") +
  labs(title="Coastlines of Africa") +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust=0.5)
  )

# note that this includes the linestring around the red sea; we want to clip this
# we will accomplish this by building a buffer zone around the african border, then intersecting that with the coastlines we generated above
buffer_zone <- st_buffer(sf.africa, dist = 20000)

# now an intersection b/w a buffer zone and the coastlines
sf.coastlines_africa2 <- st_intersection(sf.coastlines_africa, buffer_zone)

# sanity test
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data=sf.africa, color = "white", fill = "gray") +
  geom_sf(data=sf.coastlines_africa2, color = "darkblue") +
  labs(title="Coastlines of Africa") +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust=0.5)
  )

# closest coastline to a market, as a row index
closest_coast_index <- st_nearest_feature(sf.markets_full, sf.coastlines_africa2)

# index the coastline data to access the coastline row (w/ the geom)
closest_coast <- sf.coastlines_africa2[closest_coast_index,]

# find distance b/w closest coastline and the associated marketplace
distances <- st_distance(sf.markets_full, closest_coast, by_element = T)

# convert meters to kilometers
dist_to_nearest_coast_km <- as.numeric(distances) / 1000

# append back to our marketplace simple feature object
sf.markets_full$dist_to_nearest_coast_km <- dist_to_nearest_coast_km
```


## 3. Produce 3 scatter plots relating average prices with the minimum distances

```{r}
# average price of each marketplace with the min distance
# first: aggregate prices and average their prices
sf.agg_marketprice <- sf.markets_full %>% 
  group_by(market, dist_to_nearest_coast_km, dist_to_nearest_road_km, dist_to_nearest_airport_km)  %>% 
  summarize(avg_price = mean(price))


```





```{r}
# plot 1: avg price to closest airport
ggplot(data = sf.agg_marketprice,
              aes(y=avg_price, x=dist_to_nearest_airport_km))+
  geom_jitter() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  theme_minimal()

```



```{r}
# plot 2: avg price to closest road
ggplot(data = sf.agg_marketprice,
              aes(y=avg_price, x=dist_to_nearest_road_km))+
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  theme_minimal()

```




```{r}
# plot 3: avg price to closest coastline
ggplot(data = sf.agg_marketprice,
              aes(y=avg_price, x=dist_to_nearest_coast_km))+
  geom_jitter() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  theme_minimal()
```
